Summarize the following in two sentences.

Small language models are compact neural networks that generate text, typically with between a few hundred million and a few billion parameters. Because they are small, they can run directly on laptops and phones without a network connection, which improves privacy and removes the cost of calling a remote server. The main trade-off is capability: smaller models usually know less and reason less reliably than very large ones. Engineers shrink models further through quantization, which stores each weight with fewer bits, cutting memory use and often speeding up generation at a small cost in accuracy. On phones, memory bandwidth, heat and battery life, rather than raw compute, are usually what limit how fast a model can respond.

Read the passage and answer: what are the three main constraints on running a language model on a phone, and which one limits generation speed the most?

Running a language model on a phone is different from running it on a laptop in several ways. First, memory is limited. A phone might advertise 8 GB of RAM, but the operating system, background apps and the graphics stack consume a large share, so an app can often rely on only three to four gigabytes before the system starts closing processes. The model weights must fit in that space together with the key-value cache, which grows with the length of the conversation. Second, memory bandwidth is much lower than on a laptop. To produce each new token the processor has to read essentially the entire set of model weights from memory, so the speed of generation is bounded by how many bytes per second can be moved, not by how many arithmetic operations the chip can perform. This is why generation speed barely improves when more processor threads are added, even though reading the prompt, which can be done in parallel, speeds up noticeably. Third, phones are thermally constrained. They have no fans and a small surface for shedding heat, so after a minute or two of sustained work the processor lowers its clock speed to stay cool, and generation slows down. Heavy use also drains the battery quickly. Developers respond to these limits by choosing models of about one to four billion parameters, quantizing them to four bits per weight, keeping the context window short, and sometimes using the phone's neural processing unit or graphics processor when the software supports it.
